rituals.goal: Reconnect one diagonal across a blocker.
rituals.mission: Reconnect one diagonal across a blocker.
rituals.rule: The two visible diagonal pieces are parts of one straight line.
rituals.one_rule: The two visible diagonal pieces are parts of one straight line.
rituals.play: Picture a diagonal line crossing behind a thick vertical rectangle so the middle is hidden. Judge where the far segment should continue, then notice whether the visually obvious continuation feels displaced.
rituals.twist: Keep the rectangle fixed while mentally extending the hidden line.
rituals.win: Occlusion can bias alignment judgement even when the underlying path is straight.
rituals.mindBend: Occlusion can make aligned line segments look displaced. Visual continuity is inferred through hidden space and can be systematically misjudged.
rituals.mind_bend: Occlusion can make aligned line segments look displaced. Visual continuity is inferred through hidden space and can be systematically misjudged.
rituals.safety: Use content that stays clearly manageable. Reconnect visually with your environment when flashback-like imagery appears; do not continue the task.

rituals.goal: Test whether context can bend apparent size.
rituals.mission: Test whether context can bend apparent size.
rituals.rule: The two central lines are exactly equal.
rituals.one_rule: The two central lines are exactly equal.
rituals.play: Picture two equal horizontal lines. Put inward-pointing arrowheads on the first (>—<) and outward-pointing arrowheads on the second (<—>). Notice which central line feels longer before reminding yourself they are equal.
rituals.twist: Judge the central lines, not the full arrow shapes.
rituals.win: Context changes apparent length even though the central line lengths were held equal.
rituals.mindBend: Arrowheads can distort where the endpoints of an equal line seem to sit. Apparent length is an interpretation of boundary context rather than the central segment alone.
rituals.mind_bend: Arrowheads can distort where the endpoints of an equal line seem to sit. Apparent length is an interpretation of boundary context rather than the central segment alone.
rituals.safety: Use only a mild image or thought. When greater vividness or fear appears, leave the exercise; open your eyes and take in the room.

rituals.goal: Fold, punch, unfold—and predict the holes.
rituals.mission: Fold, punch, unfold—and predict the holes.
rituals.rule: The punch passes through every folded layer.
rituals.one_rule: The punch passes through every folded layer.
rituals.play: Picture a square sheet folded in half, then in half again. Punch one mental hole away from the fold edges and unfold the sheet.
rituals.twist: Predict the full hole pattern before revealing it mentally.
rituals.win: One action on folded space expands into a symmetric pattern after unfolding.
rituals.mindBend: One punch through a folded sheet becomes several holes after unfolding. Symmetry and layer overlap are rules that let a hidden final pattern be predicted.
rituals.mind_bend: One punch through a folded sheet becomes several holes after unfolding. Symmetry and layer overlap are rules that let a hidden final pattern be predicted.
rituals.safety: Use mild manageable material only for this pass. When loss of present orientation appears, stop and bring attention to something physically present.
